title: Standardized patient: chest pain
intro: Door card: Mr. Robert Kim, 62, "chest pain". Twelve minutes, history and a focused exam. This one is played as an emergency: think about what you'd do first.

steps.say: Mr. Kim is sitting bolt upright, pale and sweaty, one fist pressed to his chest.

options.text: Introduce yourself briefly and ask, "Tell me about the pain." Keep it short: he looks unwell.
options.reply: "Like an elephant sitting on me. Started forty minutes ago, shoveling the driveway."

options.text: Take a full social history first, to build rapport.
options.reply: He grimaces. "Can we talk about the pain? It's bad."

choice.lesson: In an unwell patient, focus the history on the emergency first

history.opening: "It's a pressure, right in the middle of my chest, and it won't let up."

items.ask: When did it start, and what were you doing?

items.answer: "Down my left arm. And my jaw aches."

items.ask: Anything make it better or worse? Does it change when you breathe?
items.answer: "Resting didn't help. Breathing doesn't change it."

items.ask: Any sweating, nausea or shortness of breath?
Have you had anything like this before?
items.answer: "A bit of tightness walking uphill this month. It went away when I stopped."

items.ask: Do you have high blood pressure, diabetes or high cholesterol?
items.answer: "Blood pressure and diabetes. My cholesterol's high but I stopped the pills."

items.ask: Any heart disease in your family?
items.answer: "My dad had a heart attack at fifty-eight."

items.ask: What medicines do you take, and any allergies?
Any recent long travel, leg swelling, or coughing blood?
Any tearing pain going through to your back?

maneuvers.name: Vital signs
maneuvers.finding: BP 152/94 in both arms, HR 98 and regular, RR 20, SpO₂ 95%, temperature normal.

maneuvers.name: Listen to the heart
maneuvers.finding: Regular rhythm, normal S1 and S2, a soft S4, no murmur.

maneuvers.name: Press on the chest wall
maneuvers.finding: No tenderness: the pain isn't reproduced.

choice.prompt: He grips your arm. "Am I having a heart attack?"

options.text: "I'm worried it could be your heart. That's why we're doing an ECG right now and getting the doctor. We're not going to waste any time."
"No, you're fine. Probably a pulled muscle."
options.reply: He relaxes, wrongly. The history says otherwise.

options.text: "I can't say anything. I'm only a student."
options.reply: He looks more frightened than before.

choice.lesson: Be honest about concern while acting quickly and reassuringly

steps.question: sp_cp_aspirin_01
steps.lead: "And what does he get right now?"

feedback: "Fast, focused and kind. In the real ED, you'd have saved minutes, and minutes are muscle."
"Good. In chest pain, the ECG comes before everything but the introduction."
"Let's review the chest-pain algorithm. In ACS, time is myocardium."
